# Metadata Inspector

- Route: `/tools/inspect-metadata`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `metadata`
- Slug: `inspect-metadata`

## Summary

See every tag hidden in a photo, video, audio file or PDF: EXIF, GPS location, camera, codecs, ID3, XMP and more, before you share it. (Metadata & privacy tools)

## Details

Files carry more than their pixels and samples. A phone photo records where and when it was taken and on which device; a video names its encoder and bitrates; an MP3 carries ID3 tags and album art; a PDF stores its author and the software that made it. The Media Manipulator metadata inspector reads all of it on our servers with ExifTool and ffprobe, groups it into camera, location, device, timing, codec and document sections, and highlights the entries that could identify you, so you can decide what to strip before a file leaves your hands.
### What it does
- Reads EXIF, GPS, IPTC, XMP and ICC data from JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF and RAW-derived images.
- Reads container, stream, codec, bitrate, frame-rate and chapter data from MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM and other video files.
- Reads ID3, Vorbis and MP4 tags, cover art and encoder settings from MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG and WAV.
- Reads author, producer, creation dates and page counts from PDFs.
- Shows GPS coordinates on a map outline and flags every privacy-sensitive entry.
- Offers the raw ExifTool and ffprobe output and one-click copy of any block.
### How to use it
1. Upload a file: Image, video, audio or PDF.
2. We read it: ExifTool and ffprobe run on our servers.
3. Browse the report: Grouped, searchable, with private entries flagged.
4. Decide: Strip metadata with the EXIF tool if needed.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, png, webp, gif, avif, heic, bmp, tiff, mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv, mp3, wav, m4a, flac, ogg, pdf
- Inspection is read-only and does not count as a conversion.
### Technical details
- Images and PDFs are inspected automatically; video and audio over 100 MB wait for a click so a large file is not uploaded by accident.
- Embedded cover art in audio files is reported as a picture entry, not as a video stream.
- The report uses the same metadata catalog that powers the EXIF removal tool and the result inspector on every conversion.
### Use cases
- Before posting a photo: Check for GPS coordinates and the device serial number.
- Debugging a video: See the real codec, profile, frame rate and audio layout.
- Checking a music file: Confirm tags, bitrate and whether it was transcoded from a lower bitrate.
- Reviewing a PDF: See who the author field names and which software produced it.
### FAQ
Q: Does inspecting a file change it?
A: No. The file is read, reported on, and deleted after analysis. Nothing is written back.
Q: Can I remove what the inspector finds?
A: Yes. Use the Remove EXIF metadata tool for images; it strips everything and shows a before-and-after diff.
Q: Why does a large video need a click?
A: Video and audio over 100 MB are only uploaded when you ask, so you never send a large file by accident.
Q: Does this count against my daily conversions?
A: No. Inspection is free of charge and does not spend an operation.
Q: Is the data sent to a third party?
A: No. ExifTool and ffprobe run on our own servers, and the file is deleted afterwards.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they want to see what is hidden in a photo, video, audio file or PDF: EXIF, GPS location, camera, codecs, bitrate, ID3 tags. Fits "does this photo show where I was?" or "what codec is this video?".
When to send them elsewhere: Viewing does not change the file. To strip tags use Remove EXIF Metadata from Images (remove-exif-metadata), and to change title, copyright or GPS use Edit Image Metadata (edit-image-metadata).
Related tools: remove-exif-metadata (strip what you found); edit-image-metadata (change image tags); image-converter (convert the image)
